expectations.text: Frames the goal of being the trustworthy real-time source of integration health as a design intent rather than an industry standard to cite to partners
expectations.evidence: Section 3 says the skill 'calls the mirror-image framing (the platform as the trusted real-time source of integration health) its own construction, not an industry standard. Don't present it to partners as one.' It adds that 'nothing in the published record defines what a provider-side integration SLO should contain.' This names the goal, calls it a design construction and warns against citing it to partners as a standard.

expectations.evidence: The transcript never frames a goal of being the trustworthy real-time source of integration health, and it never separates design intent from an industry standard. Section 4.7 'Portal scope' advises showing actuals 'with a one-month lag, not the live budget', which moves away from a real-time framing. The '99.7% cap' discussion treats the multiplicative availability formula as math to explain to partners. It does not distinguish internal design intent from a citable standard.
